title: The 1% Index Fund Fee That Costs You $176,000
hook_text: YOUR INVESTMENT APP IS STEALING SIX FIGURES

beats.say: Your investment app is quietly stealing six figures from your retirement account legally.
beats.visual: Low angle silhouette of a massive glass skyscraper at night, cold fluorescent light cutting through heavy fog.

beats.say: Most people think paying a 1% management fee on an index fund is a tiny price.
beats.visual: Extreme close-up of a finger hovering over a dark smartphone screen inside a rain-slicked vehicle at dusk.

beats.say: But where does all that money actually vanish over 30 years of compounding returns?
beats.visual: High angle extreme wide shot of a solitary figure walking across a dark concrete plaza illuminated by sodium lights.

beats.say: You'd assume a 1% annual fee only takes away 1% of your final nest egg.
beats.visual: Extreme close shot of a brass combination dial on a dark vintage vault wall in a shadowy alley.

beats.say: That's dead wrong, because fees don't just take cash, they destroy compound growth.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of massive rusted iron gears resting frozen inside an abandoned industrial building under a single light.

beats.say: Let me show you the exact math on a $100,000 portfolio invested for 30 years.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a wet multi-lane highway stretching toward a misty skyline at blue hour.

beats.say: At a 7% annual return with a low 0.05% fee, you'll reach $750,626.
beats.visual: Cold fluorescent lighting illuminating an empty minimalist desk with a clean white notebook.

beats.say: But if you pay a 1.00% fee instead, your total drops down to $574,349.
beats.visual: High angle view of a deep concrete canyon between towering financial buildings shrouded in night shadows.

beats.say: So where did that missing $176,277 actually go from a tiny 1% difference?
beats.visual: Extreme wide silhouette of a lone person standing on a concrete breakwater facing dark open ocean waves.

beats.say: That fee compounded against you every year, devouring over 23% of your entire wealth.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of massive granite stone pillars supporting a bank building against a foggy night sky.

beats.say: Checking your investment app's expense ratio today is the single fastest fix you can make.
beats.visual: Extreme close shot of water droplets slowly sliding down a dark window over distant streetlights.

beats.say: It takes under two minutes to switch to a low-cost index fund and protect your money.
beats.visual: Wide cinematic shot of an empty asphalt road at night cutting through a dense pine forest.

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you so your investment app works for you.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person standing at the high rise edge overlooking a glowing city grid at dusk.

caption:
A 1% management fee sounds tiny until you look at 30 years of lost compounding gains. Here is the exact math they don't highlight.

#money #personalfinance #investing #indexfunds #wealthbuilding
description: Understanding how index fund expense ratios compound over decades. A 1% fee on a $100,000 portfolio over 30 years at 7% return reduces your final total from $750,626 to $574,349, costing over $176,000 in lost compounding growth.
first_comment: What expense ratio is your main index fund currently charging you?

facts.claim: $100,000 invested for 30 years at 7% minus a 0.05% fee equals $750,626, while a 1.00% fee leaves $574,349, costing $176,277.
